sections.transition: Timpani roll swells into the crashing doom downbeat of the sam

sections.intent: State the heavy Masitkhani gat head locked with crushing doom power chords
sections.transition: Sitar pulls a slow meend down toward mandra Dha

sections.intent: Brood deeply in the mandra octave exploring the low vakra Dha and Pa
sections.transition: Snare roll drives an ascent back toward the mukhada sam

sections.intent: Re-establish the mukhada hook with added orchestral choir and rhythmic weight
sections.transition: Choir and guitars hang on a suspended chord lifting into the high octave

sections.intent: Soar into the taar register reaching taar Sa with royal brass fanfares
sections.transition: Drum fill accelerates the pulse seamlessly into rapid taan subdivision

sections.intent: Unleash rapid chaugun taan spirals driven by full double-kick thunder and symphonic tutti

seed_riff.reasoning: The riff grounds the Darbari motif in doom weight: a massive 3-beat Sa chord leaves a beat of silence for breathing, then chugs through komal ga and ma, moving to Pa and resolving from komal ni and dha back to Re before the sam.

phrase_plan.climax_and_sam: peaks on madhya Pa during the mukhada surge before resolving through g m R to land heavy and grounded on sam Sa

seed_head.idea: A ponderous, heavy Darbari Masitkhani gat head landing deep on Sa, swinging through mandra komal ga andolan

energy_arc:
Intro: Somber, expansive orchestral and sitar meditation emerging from the drone (2/10)
Mukhada 1: Crushing doom riff drops beneath the royal Masitkhani theme (6/10)
Manjha: Murky descent into the lowest depths with heavy tom rolls (5/10)
Mukhada 2: Massive, triumphant return of the main gat hook (7/10)
Antara: Ascending orchestral brass and soaring sitar reaching into the taar octave (8/10)
Taan Long: Driven, thunderous symphonic metal peak with relentless chaugun taans (10/10)
Outro: Lingering power chord resonance decaying into the tanpura drone (3/10)

rhythm_section.reasoning: Darbari Kanada in a slow, crushing Doom Metal framework (64 bpm, Teentaal = 16 beats). The arrangement strictly supports the sitar's emotional architecture. Section 0 (Intro) has no rhythm section to allow the deep mandra alap to emerge over ambient orchestral drone. Section 1 (Mukhada) establishes the heavy recurring chord pattern aligned with the harmony plan (S power 8 | P power 4 | d power 2 | S power 2): massive sustained power chords anchored by low 8th-note palm-muted chugs and a 16th-note turnaround resolving onto sam, repeated via same_as in Section 3. Section 2 (Manjha) follows the dark descent into mandra Dha and Pa; the guitar sustains modal roots S power 8 | P power 8, answering the sitar's rest at beats 12-16 with a menacing low chug and slide. Section 4 (Antara) moves to the higher register (+1 on guitar) using sparse ringing chords on m and P without chugs to give the soaring sitar complete harmonic space. Section 5 (Taan Long) ignites the climax: relentless driving chugs on low S and P pedals locking with double-kick thunder while staying harmonically grounded. Section 6 (Outro) concludes with a monumental, decaying low S power chord ringing into silence alongside the tanpura.

parts.role: Mukhada gat head accompaniment: heavy doom power chords anchored by chugs and a half-step grind turnaround into sam
Manjha descent: deep modal pedal on S and P, ringing during sitar oscillations and answering its tail rest
Mukhada reprise: identical gat head power chord progression with orchestral choir
Antara: sparse soaring high-register ringing power chords (+1) on m and P beneath the taar register sitar
Taan long climax: driving doom engine on low pedal roots S and P pushing the rapid chaugun spirals
Outro: final massive crashing low Sa power chord resonating with distortion feedback into eternity
